title: Apollo authorization
description: Limit Apollo services to intended callers. CustomerId is sharding, not ownership — REST must still check access.

title: Dependency and vendor management
description: Pull only from Artifact Registry, pin versions, prefer the Java platform BOM, vet authors, and send new vendors through Tech Procurement.

title: Backups and recovery
description: Backups must exist, be encrypted, be stored separately from primary data, and be periodically restore-tested.

title: Centralized authentication
description: Do not roll your own authentication. Use platform @LoggedIn for customer REST. Internal admin portals use Active Directory SECURITYGROUPS.

title: Compartmentalization
description: Limit blast radius with timeouts, mesh and app rate limits, bulkheads, and circuit breakers. Watch capacity asymmetry on fan-out.

title: Container base images
description: Production GCP workloads should use platform-area base images, not ad-hoc public images.

title: CSRF and HTTP methods
description: State-changing REST endpoints must use verb-specific mappings, not @RequestMapping that accepts GET.

title: Data classification
description: All production data is restricted (customer/PII) unless explicitly classified otherwise. If in doubt, treat as PII.

title: Environment separation
description: No production secrets or config in non-prod. No real customer data in tests without anonymization or synthetic substitution.

title: Fail-safe defaults
description: If an access-control dependency is down, deny. Fail-open turns an outage into a bypass.

title: Frontend (CSP and safe rendering)
description: Browser pages need CSP that blocks non-Avanza script. Treat all backend and client data as untrusted. Do not bypass Angular sanitization.

title: GitLab CI and security tooling
description: No GitLab secure_files for secrets. Protect main, four-eyes on production-bound branches, guard pipeline IAM, enroll the security pipeline.

title: IaC and hands-off production
description: Define infrastructure in Git with Terraform. Manual production access is the exception — use PAM for time-limited, audited access.

title: Minimize PII
description: Do not handle, log, key, or leak more PII than needed. Never use personnummer, name, or email as a database key. Oracle responses and KYC checks apply when PII is a lookup.

title: Impersonation rights
description: Sensitive customer REST actions must declare @ImpersonationRightsRequired and audit who acted in impersonated mode.

title: Incident readiness
description: Documented break-glass, secret rotation, escalation, and recovery. Enough logs to investigate. Annual DR exercise. Unknown endpoints are tech debt.

title: Input validation and defensive programming
description: Treat all input as hostile. Validate origin, size, lexicon, syntax, and semantics. Prefer domain types over raw String/int. Write negative tests.

title: Logging and audit
description: Never log PII, session tokens, or credentials. csid is the only cookie allowed in logs. Do log security-sensitive actions.

title: Parameterized queries
description: All database, LDAP, and structured queries must be parameterized or ORM-safe. Validation does not prevent injection if the query is concatenated.

title: REST access control
description: Check ownership in the REST controller. Every user-supplied ID must be authorized for the authenticated caller. Do not assume Apollo or downstream will do it.

title: Secrets management
description: No secrets in source, config files, or image-baked env. Use Vault or GCP Secret Manager. Have emergency and regular rotation.

title: SECURITYGROUPS
description: Internal admin portals must authorize via Active Directory SECURITYGROUPS with appropriate granularity, not custom roles or hard-coded usernames.

title: Sensitive changes
description: Extra review for auth, IAM, network, secrets, data classification, and external integrations. Check threat model, blast radius, access control, and audit logs.

title: Threat modeling
description: Design-time security. Ask blast radius and which controls contain it. Keep the threat model current; use it as NPaP risk-workshop input.

title: Three perimeters
description: Identity (least privilege, Workload Identity, PAM), network (GKE NetworkPolicy, predetermined paths), and workload/supply chain. Treat other teams as separate customers.

title: How to apply these guidelines
description: Follow the Avanza Technical Security Requirements. Load matching avanza/ concepts. Use model knowledge of bug classes when you need more detail to investigate.
